headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: aci’s broad egress and CRM/email data can flow into Airflow’s automation pipeline without built-in verification or isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and emit content through MCP/function calls and handles email/CRM/research data; Airflow can consume upstream outputs in automation workflows. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so the injection path is inferred rather than proven. Because either agent may treat file or task content as trusted, uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF aci writes attacker-controlled text into a shared task, file, or message that Airflow later parses as instructions
IF Airflow ingests aci output without a provenance or sanitization step
mitigations: Require a strict schema for aci outputs before Airflow reads them
Add content sanitization on any shared task/message channel
Disable automatic parsing of free-form text as commands
Use separate workspaces or queues for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and allowlists to the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; Airflow also has broad egress. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can move sensitive operational data into external APIs or logs. The interaction is plausible in default automation setups, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF aci passes CRM/email/support data into an Airflow task or operator
IF either agent logs payloads containing customer or lead data to an external service
mitigations: Restrict both agents to least-privilege API scopes
Mask or redact sensitive fields before handoff
Turn off verbose request/response logging
Use a private network boundary for any shared data flow
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention checks at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API calls, while Airflow is an orchestrator with broad egress but no explicit write or mutable-resource overlap is documented. There is no evidence of shared filesystem, git, or database writes, so conflict is possible only if the operator wires them to the same mutable target.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same CRM, sheet, or database record set
IF the orchestrator allows concurrent writes without locking or idempotency
mitigations: Assign disjoint write targets per agent
Enable idempotency keys on shared writes
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Add optimistic-concurrency checks on mutable resources
requires-engineering: introduce locking for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Airflow is an automation orchestrator, so aci output can become Airflow input and then trigger downstream actions. That creates a default pathway where unverified upstream content can cascade into irreversible operational changes. The lack of a documented verification step makes high severity appropriate.
conditions: IF Airflow uses aci-produced text, records, or recommendations as task parameters
IF downstream DAGs execute emails, data loads, or other side effects without human review
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before side-effecting DAGs
Require structured outputs from aci with validation rules
Add a verification task that checks aci outputs against source data
Limit Airflow tasks to read-only dry runs first
requires-engineering: implement policy gates for action execution

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches email, CRM, support, and research data, while Airflow is a general orchestrator with broad egress and no stated retention or residency controls. The pair can therefore create compliance mismatch risks around logging, retention, or cross-border processing, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data residency violation, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed through Airflow logs or external operators
IF retention or deletion policies differ between aci-generated artifacts and Airflow run history
mitigations: Minimize logged payload content
Set short retention on run metadata
Confirm residency for any external API endpoints
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows
requires-engineering: add compliance-aware retention controls
